hook: Was kein Neurologe sagt: 3 Enzyme & Ihr Nervenbrennen (What no neurologist tells you: 3 enzymes and your burning nerves)
claim: NerveSana is a German-language nerve-pain capsule from the '-Sana' product family, with alpha-lipoic acid, magnesium bisglycinate, curcuminoids and CoQ10. The page criticizes prescription nerve-pain drugs (gabapentin and pregabalin) as 'numbing you like a zombie'.
story: It cites Ikaria research by a 'Dr. Elena Papadakis, neurologist at the University of Athens', whom we couldn't verify. It also quotes a symptom-score result (63.5% vs 38.4% placebo) that resembles published alpha-lipoic acid trials rather than a study of NerveSana.
ing_note: Magnesium is in the bisglycinate form. Amounts aren't shown in text.
price_note: NerveSana is sold in euro packages at roughly €47–69 per bottle depending on the package; a 3-bottle package is shown at €177. Totals appear on the order page.
refund_note: The page refers to both 60- and 90-day guarantees; check which applies at checkout.
checks: Alpha-lipoic acid at 600 mg a day has genuine evidence for diabetic nerve pain (the SYDNEY and ALADIN trials).
Whether NerveSana provides 600 mg isn't stated.
Discouraging prescribed medicines like gabapentin and pregabalin is risky; stopping them suddenly can cause withdrawal and seizures.
The 'raw material shortage' and 'waiting list of 247 people' are pressure tactics.
pros: Contains alpha-lipoic acid, the best-studied supplement for nerve pain
verdict: NerveSana's main ingredient is a sensible choice, but its marketing is not. Don't stop prescribed nerve-pain medicines without your doctor. If you want to try alpha-lipoic acid, ask your doctor about a standard 600 mg product, especially if you have diabetes, since it can lower blood sugar.
